rationale: All three review lenses passed with no critical/major findings. Blind lens: clean — useSnapshot migration is correct, aria-expanded addition is correct, vite.config.ts fallback is safe. Edge-case lens: clean — confirmed useSnapshot returns a live reactive snapshot eliminating the old subscribe-outside-useEffect memory leak, empty useEffect dependency array is correct (handler closes over appInfoStore directly, no stale reference), vite.config.ts change is dev-server-only with safe fallback. Acceptance lens: AC1–AC3, AC5–AC6 all pass; AC4 (NVDA runtime announcement) is partial because runtime AT behaviour is inherently not automatable — the implementation is correct per ARIA spec and all necessary attributes are present and reactive. AC4 partial is deferred (not a code defect). Confidence set to medium due to the one deferred partial AC. 0 patch/decision_needed findings; 0 dismissed.

business_review.criterion: AC1: Button has aria-label="Hide Sidebar" when sidebarExpanded === true
business_review.evidence: aria-label={isOpen ? 'Hide Sidebar' : 'Open Sidebar'} set in JSX; test 'has aria-label "Hide Sidebar" when expanded' verifies

business_review.criterion: AC2: Button has aria-label="Open Sidebar" when sidebarExpanded === false
business_review.evidence: Same ternary expression covers collapsed case; test 'has aria-label "Open Sidebar" when collapsed' verifies

business_review.criterion: AC3: Button has aria-expanded={sidebarExpanded} reflecting current state
business_review.evidence: aria-expanded={isOpen} added to button JSX; tests verify both true and false values and state-change rerenders

business_review.criterion: AC4: After activation, NVDA announces updated name and role
business_review.evidence: ARIA attributes (aria-label, aria-expanded) are correctly set and update reactively via useSnapshot; implementation is correct per ARIA spec
business_review.gap: Runtime AT announcement is inherently not automatable — deferred to manual QA verification

business_review.criterion: AC5: Keyboard shortcut (Ctrl+B) continues to work
business_review.evidence: keydown handler preserved unchanged; useEffect dependency array change to [] is safe (handler reads appInfoStore directly); tests cover Ctrl+B and Meta+B

business_review.criterion: AC6: No regressions in sidebar toggle behaviour
business_review.evidence: useSnapshot replaces buggy subscribe pattern (which leaked subscriptions on every render); click-toggle test verifies toggleSidebar called on click; no regressions identified by any lens
